description: The attacker's choice of WEAPON RESOLUTION ORDER inside one fight activation (11e 04.03: 'select one weapon targeting that unit that has not yet been used to make attacks'). The engine has always resolved a unit's assignments front-to-back — FightPhase._staged_fight_* steps them as 'Weapon N of M' and RulesEngine.resolve_melee_attacks loops the same array — but the player could not SET that order: it fell out of the loadout-section build order in AttackAssignmentDialog._rebuild_assignments(), so the Boss Nob's Big choppa always swung before the Boyz' Choppas simply because his section was built first. Order is a real decision because damage never carries between models and 05.04 forces each hit onto an already-wounded model where possible, so a big-damage profile resolved after the chip attacks gets soaked by a model that is already nearly dead. The fixture is the T6 tutorial's ATTACHED unit — Warboss (Power klaw + attack squig) leading a Boyz mob with a Boss Nob — so the plan spans three loadout sections across two components. This scenario drives the new reorder rows: (1) the dialog opens on the build order, Big choppa → Choppa → Power klaw; (2) OrderRow1's real ▲ button promotes the Choppa line and the numbered rows renumber; (3) splitting the Boy section afterwards REBUILDS the whole assignment array from the sections, and the hand-picked order survives — the promoted Choppa stays first, the Big choppa stays behind it, and the brand-new Close combat weapon line lands beside its section-mate instead of at the bottom; (4) Fight! hands the engine that exact order, so staged resolution runs Choppa → Close combat weapon → Big choppa → Power klaw, with the Extra Attacks attack squig appended last as it always is. Before the rows existed this same plan could only ever resolve Big choppa first.

steps.comment: the first-run 'First time 'ere?' nudge covers the menu on a fresh user-data dir; tolerant no-op once it has been seen
acknowledge the lesson's intro instructor card so the Pile In step arms

steps.script:
var u = GameState.state["units"]["U_BOYZ_T"]
var n = 0
for m in u["models"]:
	if str(m.get("model_type", "")) == "boy":
		m["melee_loadout"] = ["Choppa", "Close combat weapon"]
		n += 1
u["_loadout_checked"] = true
return n
steps.comment: SETUP-ONLY PRIVILEGE (same stamp fight_loadout_groups_split_11e uses): the tutorial roster buys the mob nothing but choppas, so the Boy section holds one weapon and cannot split into a third line. Stamp the two-weapon melee_loadout the engine itself writes during loadout resolution — same key, same shape. Everything downstream (grouping, the order rows, the reorder, the submitted assignments, the engine's staged resolution) is the real path.
11e pile-in: five Boyz start outside engagement range, so the lesson requires a real pile-in before anyone can fight

SELECT_FIGHTER on a unit with a CHARACTER raises the Epic Challenge prompt first, and that stratagem decision gates the attack-assignment dialog. Decline it via its real button; tolerant no-op if the prompt is not offered.
the dialog opens on the BUILD order — the Boss Nob's section is built first, so his Big choppa resolves first by accident of construction, not by choice
NEW UI: one reorderable row per weapon line — this is the affordance that did not exist
rows are numbered in resolution order and name the weapon (each row also carries its target, model count and E[D])
promote the Boyz' Choppa line above the Boss Nob's Big choppa — a real button press on the real row
NEW CAPABILITY: the attacker picks which profile resolves first (11e 04.03). Before this the array order was whatever the section build produced and no click could change it.
the rows renumber, so the player can read the resolution order straight off the dialog
the ends of the list cannot walk off it
now edit the PLAN underneath the order: splitting the Boy section rebuilds the whole assignment array from the sections

the hand-picked order SURVIVES the rebuild: the promoted Choppa line is still first, the Big choppa still last, and the brand-new Close combat weapon line lands beside its section-mate rather than being exiled to the bottom

THE POINT: the engine resolves in the player's order. Staged resolution steps these front-to-back as 'Weapon 1 of 3' … 'Weapon 3 of 3', so the Big choppa now swings LAST — the inverse of what this same plan produced before the rows existed.
